Does agreement among nine LLMs tell you whether a logic formula matches its sentence?

Each sentence is translated into first-order logic by nine LLMs. A candidate's peer agreement score is the reliability-weighted share of the other systems' formulas that an SMT solver proves equivalent to it, after a vocabulary alignment that never reads predicate names. Weights come from a one-coin Dawid–Skene model fitted without labels, and the configuration was frozen on 700 development sentences before the 450 fresh sentences shown here were scored.

Every chart below is drawn from the run's result files. Use the controls to test each claim yourself.

2 · What does it add to baselines that read the text?

Stack the score on a base of judge, roundtrip and structural scores, then measure the cross-fitted AUROC gain.

Peer agreement minus its neighbours (panel labels, ΔAUROC in the same stack)

A placebo random feature added the same way is shown for scale. On panel labels the gain's 95% interval touches zero, and the score does not beat binary Dawid–Skene agreement.

3 · When do shared errors break agreement?

Replace k of the 8 peers with copies of a wrong formula and see whether the faithful candidate still outscores the error.

Real data: detection by the peer weight on wrong meanings

Fresh set, split by whether the sentence's largest equivalence cluster is faithful (panel labels)

Controlled test on 200 development sentences, 560 items per k, with alignment levels L1 and L2 only. Detection is the probability that the faithful formula scores above the mutant. On the fresh set, agreement drops below chance when the majority is wrong, while the judge is unaffected.

7 · Browse the 4,050 formalizations

Pick a sentence and compare its nine formulas, their scores and both labels.

Peer agreement lies in [0, 1] (blank when fewer than two peers are comparable). Judge is the gemini-2.5-flash score. Modal marks membership of the sentence's heaviest equivalence cluster. Solver label: equivalence to the audited gold. Panel label: blinded three-LLM majority, available for 256 sampled candidates. The relation counts give the solver's verdict against each peer.
